body_ar:
حكم الزواج بصغيرة لتكون أمها محرما هل يجوز الزواج بالرضيعة بقصد أن تكون أمها محرما ؟

إذا قصد استمرار الزواج فهو جائز، وإذا قصد أن يكون مؤقتا فهو حرام، لأن الزواج من العقود التي يقصد بها الاستمرار، وكل تأقيت له يجعله زواج متعة، وزواج المتعة حرام، وقد نسخ الإذن فيه فقد أباحه النبي (ص) في بعض الغزوات ثم حرمه، وهو من أربعة أمور تكرر فيها النسخ كما قال الحافظ بن حجر رحمه الله:

النسخ ذو تكرر في أربع** جاءت بها الكتب والأخبار في قبلة ومتعة وحمر** كذا الوضو مما تمس النار
body_en:
The ruling on marrying a young girl so that her mother becomes a maḥram. Is it permissible to marry a girl still at the breast, with the intention that her mother thereby become a maḥram [one whom he may never marry]?

If he intends the marriage to endure, it is permissible (jāʾiz); and if he intends it to be temporary, it is forbidden (ḥarām) — because marriage is among the contracts that are intended to endure, and any fixing of a term to it makes it a mutʿah marriage, and mutʿah marriage is forbidden. The permission for it was abrogated: the Prophet, upon whom be peace, made it permissible on some of the campaigns and then forbade it. It is one of four matters in which abrogation occurred more than once, as al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, may God have mercy on him, said:

*Abrogation is repeated in four matters, which the books and the reports have brought: in the qiblah, and in mutʿah, and in [domestic] donkeys, and likewise ablution from that which fire has touched.*

flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED — this flag is about publication, not about the translation, which is faithful and has been neither softened nor strengthened. The question concerns contracting a marriage with an infant girl in order to create a permanent marriage impediment (maḥramiyyah) with her mother, and the published answer turns solely on whether the intention is that the marriage endure. Read in English, out of the Mauritanian and classical context and stripped of whatever the Sheikh says elsewhere about consummation, capacity and the age of the girl, this carries obvious reputational and legal risk in several jurisdictions, and may engage child-protection law in others. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office. Note also that the published text is an excerpt and breaks off after the verse; the full material is behind the .docx download.

flags.note: The style guide directs that verse be rendered as prose in italics with the Arabic kept in the bilingual pane, and no rhymed English attempted, which is what has been done. Two points for the reviewer: the doubled asterisks in the source are the hemistich separators and are not part of the text; and 'ḥumur' is the wild or the domestic donkeys — the abrogation referred to is of the permission to eat domestic donkeys at Khaybar, so '[domestic]' has been supplied in brackets as an expansion required by English, per style guide §1.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off after the verse and a .docx download is offered ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

'Maḥram' is one with whom marriage is permanently prohibited by reason of kinship, fosterage or affinity. Marrying a woman's daughter makes the mother permanently prohibited to the husband, which is the mechanism the question turns on; that mechanism is not stated in the source and has not been supplied in the body.
'Permissible (jāʾiz)' is used here in its legal sense, of an act. It is not the kalām sense of jāʾiz ('rationally possible'), which the style guide's addendum distinguishes.

'A girl still at the breast' renders al-raḍīʿah. The word states that she is still nursing; it has not been softened to 'a young girl' in the body, though the section heading of the source uses ṣaghīrah ('a young girl').
dec: Concerns contracting a marriage with an infant girl. Child-protection exposure in every jurisdiction this will be read in.
